sources.citation: Dutta, Sukanya. 2023. A sketch study on tense and aspects of Tai-Khamyang. Journal of English Language and Literature (JOELL) 10(3): 56-62. doi:10.54513/joell.2023.10307
sources.note: Nothing; tense/aspect morphosyntax only ('Most of the verbs in Khamyang are monosyllabic').

sources.citation: Dutta, Sukanya. 2019 (uploaded to Shodhganga 2025). A descriptive grammar of Tai Khamyang: an endangered language of Assam. PhD thesis, Assam University, Silchar, Dept. of Linguistics (guide Kh. Dhiren Singha). Ch. 3 Phonology, pp. 22-71.
sources.note: Nothing. Ch. 3 covers 9 vowels, 15 consonants, sec. 3.2 Tone (six tones after Morey and Chetia; only three now in regular use), sec. 3.4 phonotactics and mono-/disyllabic syllable patterns. The words 'stress' and 'accent' do not occur in chapters 1-6.

sources.citation: Konwar, Darpanjit. 2019 (re-deposited 2022 as handle 10603/471894). Khamyang aru Phake bhashar dhvanitattva: ek sangbahanik bishleshan [Phonology of the Khamyang and Phake languages: an acoustic analysis]. PhD thesis, Dibrugarh University, Dept. of Assamese (guide Arpana Konwar). In Assamese. Ch. 5 'abibhajya dhvani' (suprasegmentals), pp. 235-274.
sources.note: No Assamese text; contents and ch. 5 scanned (tesseract asm, 300 dpi). TOC: ch. 3 vowels, ch. 4 consonants (formants, F0, duration), ch. 5 = 5.1 tone (tonal duration, F0, formants) and 5.2 syllable (syllable duration). No stress section. Ch. 5 p. 235: 'In this research work the tone and syllable of the Khamyang and Phake languages are discussed'; the word shvasaghat 'stress' appears only in two general definitions (list of suprasegmentals p. 235; 'the syllable nucleus always carries relative stress and tone', p. 254). No Khamyang stress-placement statement.

sources.citation: Konwar, Darpanjit. 2019/2022. Khamyang aru Phake bhashar dhvanitattva: ek sangbahanik bishleshan. PhD thesis, Dibrugarh University. Introduction and ch. 1 (sec. 1.6.1 'linguistic characteristics of the Khamyang language', pp. 17-70) -- already saved, not yet scanned.
sources.note: Only the contents and the suprasegmental chapter were scanned; the general-characteristics section might carry a passing remark on stress or on the (non-)role of prominence. Low expected yield, but the files are already held by the project.

sources.citation: Chetia, Madhumita. 2014. Tai Khamyang bhasha: barnanatmak adhyayan [The Tai Khamyang language: a descriptive study]. PhD thesis, Dibrugarh University, Dept. of Assamese (guide Bhim Kanta Boruah). In Assamese. Part 1 Phonology: ch. 1 vowels and tone pp. 35-53, ch. 2 consonants and syllable pp. 54-68.
sources.note: No text; contents, ch. 1 and ch. 2 scanned with tesseract asm. TOC has no stress section; sec. 1.9 tone (six tones, citing Aimya Khang Gohain and Morey 2005:161); the scanned of ch. 1-2 contains no stress term (svaraghat / balaghat / shvasaghat / 'stress').

sources.citation: Morey, Stephen. 2014. Studying tones in North East India: Tai, Singpho and Tangsa. Language Documentation & Conservation 8: 637-671.
sources.note: Khamyang is not mentioned; the iambic/stress remarks concern Turung Singpho and Tangsa.

sources.citation: Morey, Stephen. 2005. The Tai languages of Assam: a grammar and texts. Pacific Linguistics 565. Canberra: ANU. Sec. 6.4 'Some preliminary observations on Khamyang phonology', pp. 165-174; sec. 4.2.1, p. 81.
sources.note: The Khamyang sketch (consonants, vowels, vowel reduction of function words, six tones, Table 6.77) says nothing about stress. The book's only stress statement is general, p. 81 (p. 105): 'In the present study of the Tai languages of Northeast India, the level of prosodic analysis undertaken by Noss has not been possible and remains an area for further research.' Remarks on unstressed function words and unstressed loan-word syllables (pp. 121-122, 133-134, 156) concern Phake and Aiton, not Khamyang.

sources.citation: Morey, Stephen. 2005. Tonal change in the Tai languages of Northeast India. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 28(2): 139-202. Sec. 3.4 Khamyang.
sources.note: Khamyang six-tone box (same as PL565 Table 6.77); nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Grierson, G. A. 1904. Linguistic Survey of India vol. II: Mon-Khmer and Siamese-Chinese families. Calcutta. Nora (= Khamyang) sketch and specimens.
sources.note: The Nora sketch (Prodigal Son + riddles from the Sibsagar Deputy Commissioner) lists orthographic differences from Khamti and one uncertain tone sign; no accent or stress statement.
